# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel throughout the migration (dual-run architecture), allowing reconciliation and rollback at every stage. Migration proceeds in four phases, each gated by an explicit entry criterion. The legacy system remains fully active and authoritative-fallback until well after the final user batch has been migrated and validated — decommissioning is explicitly out of scope for this plan and must not occur in the same phase as the last migration batch.

---

## Phase 1: Internal & Canary Cohort (0.25% — ~100 users)

**Population:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in volunteer customers with low billing complexity (single subscription, no active disputes, standard payment method).

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full integration testing in staging, including a successful dual-write/reconciliation dry run against a synthetic dataset of 10,000 records with 100% field-level parity; on-call runbook and rollback tooling are signed off by engineering and support leads.

**Activities:** Enable dual-run for this cohort. Compare invoices, tax calculations, and payment postings between old and new systems for every billing cycle in this phase. Manual review of 100% of transactions.

---

## Phase 2: Early Adopter Segment (5% — ~2,000 users)

**Population:** Randomly sampled active accounts stratified across plan types, geographies, and payment methods (excluding highest-value enterprise accounts).

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed at least one full billing cycle with invoice/payment discrepancy rate ≤0.1%, zero critical (P0/P1) incidents, and support ticket volume for migrated users not exceeding 1.5x the baseline rate for non-migrated users.

**Activities:** Continue dual-run and reconciliation, now sampling 20% of transactions for manual audit rather than 100%. Begin automated discrepancy alerting. Support team briefed and staffed for elevated ticket volume.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability Ramp (35% — ~14,000 users)

**Population:** Broad rollout across remaining customer segments in weekly waves of ~5%, excluding the highest-complexity accounts (multi-entity billing, custom contracts, active legal/dispute holds), which are reserved for Phase 4.

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 sustained for ≥14 days with discrepancy rate ≤0.05%, no unresolved P0/P1 incidents, customer-reported billing complaints not exceeding 2x baseline, and reconciliation automation validated to require no manual sampling beyond 5% of transactions.

**Activities:** Automated reconciliation with daily discrepancy reports. Weekly go/no-go review before each wave. Old system remains system-of-record for payment retries and dispute handling for any account not yet migrated.

---

## Phase 4: Final Batch & Complex Accounts (59.75% — ~23,900 users)

**Population:** All remaining users, including high-complexity and enterprise accounts requiring white-glove migration support.

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete with cumulative discrepancy rate ≤0.05% across all migrated users, dedicated migration concierge team trained and staffed for complex-account edge cases (proration, custom billing terms, multi-currency), and a documented rollback path validated for enterprise contracts.

**Activities:** Migrate remaining users in scheduled batches with individualized support for complex accounts. Dual-run continues through this phase and for a mandatory post-migration stabilization period afterward. **Old system decommissioning is explicitly deferred to a separate, later phase** — not included in this rollout plan — and requires its own entry criteria (e.g., minimum 60-day stable dual-run with zero discrepancies across 100% of migrated accounts, full audit sign-off, and finance/compliance approval).

---

## Risks

RISK: Invoice/payment discrepancies between old and new systems cause incorrect customer billing | Run mandatory dual-write reconciliation with automated diffing before and during each phase; halt phase progression on threshold breach | Engineering Lead (Billing Platform)
RISK: Payment processor or tax-calculation integration behaves differently under production load than in staging | Load-test new system at 2x expected peak volume before Phase 3; maintain feature flag to instantly reroute traffic back to old system per account | SRE/Infrastructure Lead
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during ramp phases | Pre-brief and staff support team ahead of each phase, define escalation runbook, cap weekly migration wave size in Phase 3 to match support capacity | Head of Customer Support
RISK: Data corruption or loss during account migration (e.g., missing payment methods, subscription state mismatch) | Snapshot and checksum-validate every account record pre- and post-migration; require reversible migration scripts with tested rollback per batch | Data Migration Engineering Lead
RISK: Regulatory/compliance failure (e.g., incorrect tax handling, PCI scope gaps) in new system | Independent compliance review and sign-off required before Phase 1 entry and again before Phase 4 entry | Compliance & Risk Officer

---

## Halt Metric

If the **invoice/payment discrepancy rate for migrated users exceeds 0.5% in any rolling 24-hour window**, or **P0/P1 incidents attributable to the new billing system exceed 2 in any 7-day period**, the rollout is automatically halted, no further accounts are migrated, and the on-call engineering lead must approve resumption after root-cause remediation.

PHASES: 4
